title: Sold your flat, less cash than expected?

lines.say: You sell your flat for 600,000 dollars. You expected a big cheque. It's much smaller.
lines.cap: you sell for *$600,000.* the cheque is *much smaller*

lines.say: Every CPF dollar you used for your home must go back to your CPF account first.
Plus the interest it would have earned: 2.5% a year, compounded.
Used 200,000 dollars over 15 years? You could owe CPF close to 290,000 dollars.
lines.cap: used *$200,000?* you could owe close to *$290,000*

lines.say: It's not lost. It goes back into your own CPF. But it's not cash in hand.
lines.cap: not lost. but *not cash in hand*

lines.say: Planning your next home? Count your cash proceeds after the CPF refund, not before.
lines.cap: count your cash *after the CPF refund*

source: CPF Board. Illustration: lump sum used at the start.
caption:
Sold your flat for $600,000 but the cheque is much smaller? 🏠

Every CPF dollar you used for your home goes back to your CPF account first, plus the interest it would have earned: 2.5% a year, compounded. Used $200,000 over 15 years? You could owe CPF close to $290,000.

It's not lost: it goes back into your own CPF. But it's not cash in hand. Planning your next home? Count your cash proceeds after the CPF refund, not before.

Useful info? Follow for more 👇

Illustration assumes a lump sum used at the start. Check your figure on the CPF website.
